pageCache.pageTitle: Oakhill Church School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Oakhill Church School Vision
Love, Trust, Determination, Joy
At Oakhill Church School, we demonstrate, through love, trust, determination and joy, that our children are known, valued, and encouraged to develop an intrinsic happiness in who they are. With high expectations, challenge and curiosity, we nurture a community, where compassion and a sense of global responsibility is at the heart of all we do.
“A caring family where we grow together”
Let your light shine – Matthew 5 v 16
School Vision
We know that every child is a unique gift and is precious to God. Together, we create the Oakhill family where we are given the space and opportunities to learn, grow and flourish. Our learning and experiences are valued, purposeful and relevant for life now and in the future. We believe our journey together will equip us with the tools to unlock the
‘Best versions of ourselves’.
Our Vision
Our vision for Oakhill Church School where all children are known and valued as unique individuals, where differences are respected and celebrated. With community and childhood at the heart, our school intentionally nurtures kindness towards one another and believes that children thrive only when their wellbeing is held at the core of their journey. We believe in our children, and through imagination, high expectations and challenge, we inspire them to reach their fullest potential, and develop an intrinsic happiness in who they are.
Our Christian Values
The vision for Oakhill Church School is under-pinned by our 12 Christian values, which guide how the community relates to each other, and our environment. These Christian values can also be seen as common values, held equally by members of different faiths and no faith alike. Exploring our values, which guide our choices and reflections, over a two-year cycle, we focus on a different value each term, celebrating and discussing it in collective worship, assembly and in class.
Through linking the selected value to events on the calendar, modern day themes and engaging children with the theological underpinnings, we strive to enable Oakhill Church School to be a community that seeks to embody an ethos of living well together – preparing children for the challenges as a 21st Century citizen in Modern Britain, respecting and showing understanding of others for all that is similar and different.
This strong ethos permeates school life and the emphasis on increasing our children’s awareness of our ‘values’ is a significant factor in enhancing the pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.

Christian Distinctiveness
Love, Trust, Determination and Joy
“A caring family where we grow together”
'Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.' Matthew 5:16
At Oakhill Church School we are very lucky to have a strong relationship with All Saints’ Church. The School and Church are located only feet apart which enables the school to make full use of the facilities.
Our children lead a church service every two to three weeks in All Saints’ Church with parents and the wider community arriving to support the children in worship.
Our school families and the wider community regularly attend worship with our children and for key events in the Christian calendar the Church invites pupils and staff to join these events.
As a School we have a daily act of collective worship or assembly. This includes Teacher led worship, House assemblies and worship through singing. Over the course of the year we have a Values focus each term. This value directs the worship and themes for that term.
Our school values direct the worship themes for each half term and we use the Roots and Fruits resource to support our Christian worship and spiritual and moral development.
Our half termly values are:
Autumn 1 Generosity
Autumn 2 Compassion
Spring 1 Courage
Spring 2 Forgiveness
Summer 1 Friendship
Summer 2 Respect

Welcome
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Oakhill Church School — a small, caring rural school where every child is truly known, valued and celebrated.
At Oakhill, our children flourish within a close-knit community built on our core values of Love, Trust, Determination and Joy. These values are not just words on a page; they guide everything we do, shaping the way we learn together, care for one another, and face challenges with confidence and kindness.
As a small school with mixed-age classes, we are proud of the strong family feel that defines our community. Our children learn to support one another, develop meaningful friendships across year groups, and grow in independence and responsibility. We believe this nurturing environment helps children develop a deep sense of belonging and an intrinsic happiness in who they are.
We hold high expectations for every child, encouraging curiosity, creativity and a love of learning. Through challenge and thoughtful support, we empower our pupils to believe in themselves, persevere when things are difficult, and take pride in their achievements. Compassion, respect and a sense of global responsibility are woven into daily school life, helping our children grow into thoughtful, caring citizens of the wider world.
Our beautiful rural setting provides rich opportunities for outdoor learning, reflection and exploration, and our strong Christian ethos underpins our commitment to inclusion, kindness and community.
We would be delighted to welcome you to Oakhill Church School and invite you to come and visit us. There is no better way to understand our school than to see the warmth, joy and determination of our children and staff for yourself.
We look forward to meeting you and sharing all that makes Oakhill such a special place to learn and grow.
Ms Dowley and Miss Baker

Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Oakhill Church School & Nursery is pleased to be able to provide the children of our school the opportunity to attend Breakfast Club and After School Club. These clubs may be attended on an ad hoc basis subject to availability. This childcare provision is an extension of Oakhill Church School & Nursery and therefore operates in line with the school’s ethos and values and high expectations of pupil behaviour. The wraparound care staff have been appointed for their expertise in childcare and have the necessary qualifications for safeguarding, behaviour management, first aid and food hygiene.
It is the wish of everyone involved to provide a happy and stimulating environment in which children are supported to reach their full potential. We believe that a positive partnership with parents and carers is crucial and promotes our aim to maximise the child’s learning and ensure wellbeing and well-rounded development.
Opening Hours and Fees
Oakhill Church School & Nursery Breakfast Club:
Oakhill Church School & Nursery After School Club:
Our Breakfast and After school care all runs from our Nursery. Parents will need to come to reception and press the blue doorbell and a member of the team will come to the office. Parents are welcome to use our car park for this service but please be aware of staff and children moving around the car park. Please can we ask that you park in the marked bays and not block other cars in.
Breakfast and After School sessions must be booked in advance on Arbor. This can be up to 1 hour before the session is due to start.

pageCache.text:
Phonics & Early Reading
At Oakhill we follow Read Write Inc. for phonics.
What is Read, Write, Inc.?
Read Write Inc. (RWI) is a phonics complete literacy programme which helps children learn to read fluently and at speed so they can focus on developing their skills in comprehension, vocabulary and spelling. RWI was developed by Ruth Miskin and more information on this can be found at https://ruthmiskin.com/en/find-out-more/parents/.
Order of the programme
The programme is ordered through a series of colour-coded books, each progressively introducing new letters and sounds. Children are assessed every term to review whether they are ready to progress onto the next book colour. Below, you can find the progression of book colours and the typical age-range that children will be exposed to them. You can also find, below, documents to download which identify exactly which new learning is introduced in each book colour phase.
Books Year Group Expectations
Red Ditty 1-10 Reception
Green 1-10 Reception
Purple 1-10 Reception
Pink 1-10 Reception/Year One
Orange 1-12 Year One
Yellow 1-10 Year One
Blue 1-10 Year One/Year Two
Grey 1-13 Year Two

Attendance
Dear Oakhill families
Our approach to attendance is All day, Every Day, On Time!
Being on time is a life skill and its starts at the earliest age. We ask that you contact school if there is any circumstance that you cannot bring your child to school – or you may be late. Our children start school from the minute they join Nursery and we have the expectation that they will be in every session.
Holidays in term time will not be authorised unless there are very exceptional circumstances and we ask that you book dentist and doctors appointments outside the school day.
Non attendance - The safeguarding of your children is vitally important to us and we will always undertake the most stringent safeguarding procedures to ensure that your children are safe.
We will also take good care of your children and you will be contacted if we think they are too poorly for school.
We have a dedicated team of support to help you.
Mrs Caddick is our friendly PFSA lead who supports families – she will be the first point of contact with you should we need to discuss your child’s attendance or any other needs you have as a family. She has a wealth of knowledge and is very supportive!
Mrs Swarbrooke and Miss Dowley will both greet you on the gate in the morning – accompanied by the days choice of music!
Miss Burgess our SENDCo will also be on gates every 2nd Tuesday and Wednesday should you have any SEND questions and enquiries.
Your child’s class teachers will be in touch via the school app should there be any questions regarding attendance and Behaviour for Learning.
We love celebrating great attendance and we award certificates for the best class and personal attendance!
Oakhill Attendance Policy

PTA
Oakhill PTA
Oakhill Church School & Nursery is fortunate to have an active, supportive group of parents, who are keen to promote the interests of the school. All parents with children attending Oakhill are automatically members of the Association, but we welcome any volunteers, especially our new parents. If you can spare a couple of hours of your time a few times a year, this would be greatly appreciated.
Please do come along to our future meetings to find out what we are planning this year and to share your ideas and suggestions.

School Day
Oakhill Church School arrival and collection times for Nursery and School:
Nursery hours
Drop off at 08.45 and pick up at 15.15
School hours
Arrive between 8.35 and 8.45 and be collected at 15.15
Office opening hours
The office is open between 8.30 and 15.15 to contact the school outside these hours please leave an answerphone message or send an email to [email protected].

School Meals
Our lunches are supplied by The Fabulous Lunch Company who offer delicious cooked meals using fresh ingredients, locally sourced where possible. They offer a choice of 3 meals every day, including meat, vegetarian meals and jacket potatoes as well as delicious puddings.
All children in Key Stage 1 are entitled to Universal Free School Meals, from Year 3 and up a hot meal and pudding costs £2.90 per day.
All orders for lunches are made on Arbor and need to be made 14 days in advance (rolling). If you are having any problems making a booking please contact the school office. Please note that meals can only be purchased if there is a clear/credit on your child’s account.
Menu
The menu is available to view on Arbor. Lunches must be ordered and paid for on Arbor 14 days (rolling) in advance.
All children in KS1 and Reception are entitled to Universal Free School Meals. Please register if you have not already done so – forms available from the school office or can be downloaded.
Even if your child is in KS2 you may be entitled to free school meals – please download the letter from Somerset County Council.
Packed Lunches
Oakhill Church School has a healthy eating policy. We ask that children who bring packed lunches should aim to include all food groups in their lunchbox as does school meals. NO chocolate bars, chocolate biscuits or sweets are permitted in lunchboxes. We also ask that only one item of processed food is included as these can contain extremely high levels of salt, sugar or fat. We are grateful for your support in helping your child to be healthy, active and happy!
Your child will be supplied with a pack lunch for school trips if they are in reception – year 2 or free school meals
Please note we are a nut free school

pageCache.text:
Severe Weather
Wherever possible Oakhill School will remain open. It may, however, be necessary for the school to close in the case of extreme weather conditions or there being insufficient adult supervision.
If the decision is made not to open school as a result of deteriorating conditions overnight, we will contact parents via email, Arbor and Seesaw.
If worsening weather conditions indicate that by 3.15 pm children and staff may have difficulty getting home, every attempt will be made to contact you to ask you to come and collect your children from school.
If you anticipate difficulties collecting your children later in the day due to the weather conditions, please come early and collect children from school, or telephone us to let us know what arrangements to make. The Headteacher or other authorised person will remain at school until all children have been safely collected.

Curriculum Intent and Progression of Skills
“Let Your Light Shine”
“A caring family where we grow together”
Let your light shine – Matthew 5 v 16
Roots Nursery - long term curriculum plan
Oakhill Intent Statement
At Oakhill Church School the curriculum is designed to: constantly build upon children’s prior learning, provide first hand learning experiences, allow the children to develop interpersonal skills, build resilience and become creative, critical thinkers.
Every child is recognised as a unique individual. We celebrate and welcome differences within our school community. The ability to learn is underpinned by the teaching of basic skills, knowledge, concepts and values.
We constantly provide enhancement opportunities to engage learning through using five curriculum drivers: Learning Behaviours, Global Responsibility, Well-being, Communicators and Creativity, Arts and Performance.
Our first central curriculum driver ‘Learning Behaviours’ promotes independence and positive attitudes to learning which reflect the values and skills needed to promote responsibility for life-long learning and future success.
In addition, local and global community involvement is an essential part of our curriculum as we celebrate traditions, learning new skills to enable the children to take an active role in events throughout the year. Children leave Oakhill Church School with a sense of belonging to a tightly knit community where they have the confidence and skills to make decisions, self-evaluate, make connections and become lifelong learners.
Curriculum Intent and Implementation
The curriculum at Oakhill Church School is underpinned by our vision for our children: “Together we Grow from Acorns to Oaks.”
Our Vision
Our vision for Oakhill Church School where all children are known and valued as unique individuals, where differences are respected and celebrated. With community and childhood at the heart, our school intentionally nurtures kindness towards one another and believes that children thrive only when their wellbeing is held at the core of their journey. We believe in our children, and through imagination, high expectations and challenge, we inspire them to reach their fullest potential, and develop an intrinsic happiness in who they are.
Our Christian Values
The vision for Oakhill Church School is under-pinned by our 12 Christian values, which guide how the community relates to each other, and our environment. These Christian values can also be seen as common values, held equally by members of different faiths and no faith alike. Exploring our values, which guide our choices and reflections, over a two-year cycle, we focus on a different value each term, celebrating and discussing it in collective worship, assembly and in class.
Through linking the selected value to events on the calendar, modern day themes and engaging children with the theological underpinnings, we strive to enable Oakhill Church School to be a community that seeks to embody an ethos of living well together – preparing children for the challenges as a 21st Century citizen in Modern Britain, respecting and showing understanding of others for all that is similar and different.
This strong ethos permeates school life and the emphasis on increasing our children’s awareness of our ‘values’ is a significant factor in enhancing the pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
Our Learning Behaviours
Oakhill children will become resilient to be able to deal with different challenges across the curriculum and in the wider world. They will develop the ability to solve problems without giving up. Developing the skills to work independently and as a team, they will be encouraged to reflect upon their actions, learning and opinions– evaluating ‘what went well’ and how they could improve by identifying their own next steps.
Our Key Words:
Active Learner
Creative Thinker
Team Worker
Self-manager
Our Curriculum Drivers
Global Responsibility
Oakhill children will develop an understanding about where they live and the wider world. Through learning about the world, they will understand their role in society and develop respect towards the environment, communities and all faiths. Our children will know themselves and where they come from but also look beyond Oakhill and the UK and recognize the incredible opportunities that are created by diversity and the richness of culture that there is across our planet.
Teaching our children about global issues and encouraging them to see the world through the eyes of others is of huge importance. In an increasingly interconnected world, today’s young generation need to learn to be able to engage in respectful communication with people from a wide range of different cultures and traditions.

Effective Communication
Oakhill children will develop the skills to work well with other people. They will know how to speak and listen with respect in a variety of different situations. They will become increasingly confident, eloquent and effective communicators. They will be able to express their understanding and share their learning widely in a range of ways. They will learn and apply technical and challenging vocabulary.
